question: Does the public AlphaBeta route preserve PassAction, consecutive-pass adjudication, generated semantic actions, and legal fallback behavior?
scope: Two existing deterministic local fixtures; interface and state-transition checks only, with test-only evaluators. No utility, strength, timing, or full-domain claim.

legacy_consecutive_pass_fixture.pass_adjudication: DRAW after two consecutive pass actions

pre_cancelled_root_fallback.fixture: same 4x4 pass-enabled legacy ruleset before any action

qsearch_pass_child_policy.fixture: 4x4 legacy rules with both Kings blocked by own immobile pieces; every side-to-move has only PassAction

qdepth_one.interpretation: nonterminal quiet pass is excluded from qsearch

qsearch_pass_child_policy.interpretation: Bounded interface test: qsearch includes a terminal PassAction before its depth cutoff and excludes a nonterminal quiet pass. The deliberately chosen static evaluator and one fixture do not imply utility, strength, or complete qsearch coverage.

semantic_qsearch_terminal_pass.fixture: 5x5 ExecutableSemanticRuleset from _pass_mate_ruleset(threshold=3), with both Kings blocked by own immobile pieces; two semantic action definitions remain configured but have no pieces on this position
semantic_qsearch_terminal_pass.interpretation: The public semantic-compiled executor agrees with the bounded legacy terminal-pass qsearch contract. Semantic action definitions were configured but not generated on the blocked position; this does not establish generated-semantic qsearch coverage or complete-domain equivalence.

qsearch_repetition_pass_child.fixture: 4x4 legacy pass-only rules; both Kings blocked by own immobile pieces; repetition limit3
qsearch_repetition_pass_child.interpretation: The public legacy qsearch includes the fourth pass when its complete history makes the child a repetition draw. Scores use a deliberately chosen test evaluator and are behavioral contrasts, not utility or strength estimates.

semantic_qsearch_repetition_pass_child.fixture: 5x5 ExecutableSemanticRuleset with two configured semantic action definitions, but no semantic pieces on the blocked pass-only board; repetition limit3 and no consecutive-action policy
semantic_qsearch_repetition_pass_child.interpretation: The semantic-compiled route preserves the same complete-history repetition terminal child as legacy. Semantic action definitions remain configured but are not generated by this blocked position; no claim is made about generated semantic action qsearch or full-domain equivalence.

native_semantic_qsearch_repetition_child.fixture: Existing deterministic 4x4 F/G four-cycle, reconstructed as a RuleSet and compiled through compile_legacy_ruleset_for_semantic_execution; exactly one legal semantic action at every ply

qsearch_frontier.sole_semantic_action_child: repetition (fourth occurrence under complete played history)

native_semantic_qsearch_repetition_child.interpretation: The native semantic-search kernel and independent Core agree on this translated legacy-atom semantic fixture. It is not a DSL-generated semantic action or generated-hybrid coverage, nor an all-domain, strength, or utility claim.

interpretation: No defect or production behavior change was observed. The assertions cover only the named deterministic fixtures and bounded probes. The native semantic route here is legacy-atom-derived, not DSL-generated; these results do not establish complete generated-rule-domain equivalence, fallback selection quality, search strength, or utility.

public_alphabeta_native_dispatch_pass.fixture: Existing blocked 5x5 ExecutableSemanticRuleset with two configured semantic actions, neither generated on this board; repetition limit3; test evaluator from the existing public qsearch regression

source_dispatch.player: AlphaBetaPlayer.choose_action calls run_root_search and passes the optional NativeSemanticLegalityProvider only as a legal-binding provider
source_dispatch.runtime: SearchPathRuntime appends Core-checked PassAction after successful semantic bindings; otherwise enumerates bindings in Core
source_dispatch.native_compiler: Native semantic ruleset compilation rejects pass-enabled rules
source_dispatch.scope: This public AlphaBeta entry does not route to standalone SemanticSearchEngine

public_alphabeta_native_dispatch_pass.interpretation: Both the existing ExecutableSemanticRuleset public route and a new CompiledSemanticRuleset regression safely decline Native legality for pass-enabled rules and preserve Core PassAction qsearch. The standalone Native kernel still does not support PassAction; no code change or strength claim.

native_declared_semantic_history_repetit.fixture: 4x4 typed CompiledSemanticRuleset reconstructed from the deterministic F/G cycle, with legacy F/G atoms removed and four declared F/G up/down semantic actions; each state in the 12-ply cycle has exactly one generated semantic action
native_declared_semantic_history_repetit.terminal_path: From the ply8 root, three forced mainline moves reach an ongoing frontier; its sole declared semantic action reaches the fourth occurrence and Core REPETITION.
native_declared_semantic_history_repetit.interpretation: Native and Core agree for qdepth0/1 on a true typed generated-semantic cycle. Same board/side with one versus nine history records yields qdepth1 scores400 versus0 solely at the bounded repetition boundary. No strength, utility, general support or all-domain claim.

native_action_event_terminal_audit.conclusion: No Native-supported consecutive-action terminal class distinct from pass was found. Do not construct a redundant event-class matrix.
native_action_event_terminal_audit.separate_candidate: Continuous-check repetition loss has Native terminal transition tests, but no qsearch child parity test alongside ordinary repetition qsearch controls; inspect one existing finite Shogi line before deciding whether a regression is warranted.
